ght hydrocarbons, such as naphtha and benzene, were circulated through the excha

apors from the hydrotreater went into the reactor. From the reactor, the vapors

cooling within the exchangers. The product continued on to the pressure separat
or, where the two states were separated out, along with the wash water. Wash wat
er was injected into the flow before the 55-EX-01D and after the 55-EX-01E excha
ngers to remove organic and inorganic material that might have been in the napht
ha flow. The wash water system had been down for maintenance since the beginning
of the month. The temperature of the naphtha when it left the reactor was over
250 degrees F. The temperature at the time the flow entered the 55-EX-02B exchan
ger was approximately 130 to 140 degrees F. When the flow exited the 55-EX-02A e
xchanger, the temperature was approximately 90 degrees F. The heat exchanger was
manufactured in 1971 by Heat Exchanger Service of Dutchtown, LA.

face layout and condition. The employer in this situation conducted intermittent

ignments for which training has not previously been received. It was also recomm
ended that the employer implement a safe materials handling process and associat
ed training programs.

aning the rollers located in the rear of the tractor which was in the strawberry

wards the rear of a nursery and going about 5 mph. Employee #1 was walking on th

Employee #1 was setting a sheet of plastic on top of some carpeting inside a hou
se under construction before detailing some windows at about 18 feet above the f

p against the wall below the window. He instructed a laborer to hold the bottom

ome work above. Employee #1 had successfully completed three windows and was jus

Employee #1, age 19, was next to a 14 in. high parapet, helping to land material

ny form of fall protection.

On December 1, 2005, an employee worked for a company engaged in the manufacture

uck bed, the tailgate opened up, and when it hit the ground, the employee lost h

was crushed by a bucket of a Cathead 930 Loader, when it rolled into an excavati

een pinch points. She was killed.
Employee #1, of Kaw Valley Builders, was part of a crew removing rotating biolog
ical contactors (RBCs) from the roof of the wastewater treatment plant in Beatri

. Employee #2 was swinging one of the RBC units away from the building to be set

ushed by the falling load as it landed on the cab of his crane. He suffered head

ection of the scaffold into contact with the power line.
ere was no previous report of the lift gate malfunctioning. There were no accide

At approximately 4:20 p.m. on July 30, 1999, Employee #1, age 20, was helping pr

ay squeeze. The forklift-type vehicle struck Employee #1 in the back and ran ove

loyee #1 was on the left-side of the trailer checking the connections between th
e truck and trailer, the tires, and other areas while the coworker was on the ri

he inspection of the left side of the trailer, Employee #1 was to inspect the ri

orward and Employee #1 fell to the ground. Employee #1 sustained a collapsed lun
g, broken ribs, broken bones in the left arm, and a dislocated left elbow. Emplo
yee #1 was hospitalized.
On April 27, 2001, a construction employee was operating an aerial work platform
. The employee was instructed by his supervisor to use the aerial platform to li
ft 4 ft. by 8 ft. sheets of plywood and material to the roof. At the moment the

r, a gust of wind came along. The employee in the aerial lift and work platform
reatment with her asthma reaction kit and epinephrine. When she began to have ab
dominal cramping, decompression sickness was strongly suspected and Employee #1

At approximately 12:20 p.m. on April 4, 1997, Employee #1 was installing a glass

t his wrist, severing three tendons. Employee #1 was hospitalized for surgery an

ia Steel Industries, Inc., suffered a non-serious injury when the fatty pad of t
